purpose: Exploration prompts and preparation questions; not validated capabilities, phenomenon labels, model selection or an admission contract.

time-series.title: Measurements over time
questions: What does each observation measure, in which units, and for which entity?
Are timestamps regular, irregular or asynchronous across channels?
Which gaps, exact zeros, resets and changes in collection practice must remain distinguishable?
time-series.preparation: Preserve timestamps and channel identities. Document alignment, units and missingness before choosing any resampling or scaling.

event-sequences.title: Timestamped events
questions: What defines an event, its identity and its occurrence time versus its arrival time?
Are repeated events duplicates or genuine repetitions?
Which entity and session boundaries must be preserved?
event-sequences.preparation: Keep event order, elapsed time and entity boundaries. Any binning or aggregation needs a stated rule and a check that it preserves the phenomena of interest.

relationships.title: Relationships and networks
questions: What do nodes, edges, directions and weights mean?
Do entities or relationships appear, disappear or change identity?
Are observations individual events or network snapshots?
relationships.preparation: Preserve entity mappings and relationship semantics. A graph-to-observation representation requires its own documented and tested input contract.

spatial-panels.title: Measurements across locations
questions: What are the coordinates, coordinate system, resolution and any depth or altitude axes?
Are locations fixed, moving or sampled unevenly?
Which observations are simultaneous and which only appear in the same file?
spatial-panels.preparation: Retain coordinates, measurement support, time and coverage. Do not treat arbitrary row or location order as chronology.

repeated-runs.title: Repeated experiments or operating cycles
questions: What defines a run, cycle, subject or batch boundary?
Do sampling rates, durations or experimental conditions differ?
Which measurements were available at each point within a run?
repeated-runs.preparation: Retain run boundaries and conditions. Specify alignment and state reset policy; do not concatenate independent runs into an invented continuous history.

encoded-media.title: Numerical representations of text, images or audio
questions: Which numerical representation or feature extractor is proposed, and what is its version?
Which temporal, spatial or semantic relationships does that representation preserve or discard?
Are feature definitions stable across the proposed dataset?
encoded-media.preparation: Record representation provenance and retained axes. A numerical encoding is not proof of Kirk compatibility or a useful embedding; verify a matching input contract.

unordered-samples.title: Unordered samples or static tables
questions: Are rows independent samples, or is there a genuine temporal or spatial order?
Which sample, batch and feature identities matter?
Would the proposed representation introduce an artificial ordering?
unordered-samples.preparation: Preserve sample and batch identities. Do not invent a time axis or interpret an inferred ordering as observed chronology; suitability needs separate assessment.
